findings.title: Map `reconciliation-pending` publications to exit 1.

findings.body:
**Route status-writer error text into the JSON artifact instead of stderr.**

The `status` route writes refusal text straight to `process.stderr` (`src/queue-runner/crq.ts:167`). The same route captures the markdown into the JSON artifact (`crq.ts:162-166`), so the stdout path already follows the contract. The stderr path does not. The queue-runner comment at `crq.ts:159-161` states that stdout is exactly one JSON document for every command. Under doctrine I1, a machine-mode invocation keeps stderr empty, and a failure with no result is reported as one `{ "error": ... }` object on stdout. When `runStatusWriter` refuses, the `status-writer: <label>: <message>` text reaches stderr, so machine consumers see stderr output on this path. Return that message in the error object's `message` field, and leave `process.stderr` unused on this route.
findings.title: Route status-writer error text into the JSON artifact instead of stderr.

findings.body:
**Encode `events.jsonl` lines with the producer's `json.dumps` format.**

The producer's `event()` writes `json.dumps({"at": ..., "event": kind, **data})` with default arguments. Python escapes non-ASCII text by default and separates keys and values with `", "` and `": "`. `appendEvent` uses `JSON.stringify`, which writes non-ASCII characters raw and emits no spaces. A `summary_failed` line whose `error` contains non-ASCII text therefore differs byte-wise from the producer's line. Lines with ASCII-only text also differ because of the spacing. Serialize the line with `pythonJsonText(..., { asciiOnly: true })`, as the adjacent `publishSummary` code and the sibling seam in `tickPhaseSeams.ts` already do.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
       const at = new Date(now() * 1000).toISOString().replace(/\.\d{3}Z$/, 'Z');
       await writeFile(
         join(roots.stateRoot, 'events.jsonl'),
-        `${JSON.stringify({ at, event: event.event, error: event.error })}\n`,
+        `${pythonJsonText({ at, event: event.event, error: event.error }, { asciiOnly: true })}\n`,
         { flag: 'a' },
       );
```

</details>
findings.title: Encode `events.jsonl` lines with the producer's `json.dumps` format.

findings.body:
**Require `headEntry` to be a regular file.**

`verifyReview` checks only `targetEntry.mode` at `src/adapters/crq/reviewVerify.ts:265`. `headEntry.mode` is never checked. `entries()` keeps every `ls-tree` mode, including `120000`, and `changedIntervals()` does not filter by mode.

If `base` lacks the path, a head-side symlink can reuse a blob from a regular target file. A symlink blob holds the link target path. The added symlink line can then pass the blob, line-count, and changed-interval checks, which credits a non-regular head entry.

Require both entries to be regular files:

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
-      if (targetEntry.mode !== '100644' && targetEntry.mode !== '100755') {
+      if (
+        (targetEntry.mode !== '100644' && targetEntry.mode !== '100755') ||
+        (headEntry.mode !== '100644' && headEntry.mode !== '100755')
+      ) {
```

</details>
findings.title: Require `headEntry` to be a regular file.
